questions.explanation: Chirality requires a carbon atom bonded to four different groups. In 3-methylpentane, the second carbon is bonded to a hydrogen, a methyl group, an ethyl group, and a propyl group, making it chiral.
questions.question: Which of the following is a chiral molecule?

questions.correct_answer: Primary alkyl halide, polar aprotic solvent, strong nucleophile
questions.explanation: SN2 reactions are favored by primary alkyl halides (less steric hindrance), polar aprotic solvents (which do not solvate the nucleophile), and strong nucleophiles.
options: Primary alkyl halide, polar protic solvent, weak nucleophile
Tertiary alkyl halide, polar aprotic solvent, strong nucleophile
Primary alkyl halide, polar aprotic solvent, strong nucleophile
Tertiary alkyl halide, polar protic solvent, weak nucleophile
questions.question: Which reaction conditions favor an SN2 mechanism?

questions.correct_answer: A structure with a single bond between carbon and one oxygen and a double bond to the other, with charges distributed appropriately.
questions.explanation: Resonance structures for the acetate ion show the delocalization of the negative charge across both oxygen atoms, resulting in one C-O single bond and one C-O double bond, with the negative charge being shared.
options: A structure with a single bond between carbon and one oxygen and a double bond to the other, with charges distributed appropriately.
A structure where all bonds to oxygen are single bonds and the negative charge is localized on the carbon atom.
A structure where both bonds to oxygen are double bonds.
A structure with a double bond to one oxygen and a single bond to the other, with both oxygens having a full octet and no formal charges.
